annotations.title: Gold Market Commentary: Hiking up a volcano | World Gold Council

content.text:
**Short answer: gold doesn’t look obviously undervalued here; it looks “strategically supported but tactically expensive/fully priced.”** If you already own it as a hedge, the case for holding some remains strong. If you’re asking whether it’s a bargain, I’d be cautious.

As of **June 8, 2026**, the SPDR Gold Shares ETF **GLD** is around **$396.45**, while gold miners via **GDX** are around **$79.07**. That reflects a gold market that has already priced in a lot of the bull case: geopolitical risk, reserve diversification, inflation concerns, and central-bank buying. 

### Why gold **could still be undervalued**
- **Central-bank demand remains a major structural support.** The World Gold Council reported estimated central-bank net purchases of **244 tonnes in Q1 2026**, above the previous quarter and above the five-year average. That is important because official-sector buying is less short-term/speculative than ETF flows. ([gold.org](https://www.gold.org/goldhub/research/gold-demand-trends/gold-demand-trends-q1-2026/central-banks?utm_source=openai))  
- **Dollar-reserve diversification is a real theme.** Gold’s appeal rises when investors and governments worry about fiscal deficits, sanctions risk, currency debasement, or the reliability of sovereign bonds as reserves.
- **Gold can perform well if real yields fall.** If the Fed eventually cuts rates, inflation stays sticky, or the dollar weakens, the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding gold falls.

### Why gold may **not** be undervalued
- **The price already reflects a lot of good news.** Recent World Gold Council commentary notes that gold is being pulled between supportive structural demand and pressure from higher real yields; higher policy rates and real yields traditionally weigh on gold. ([gold.org](https://www.gold.org/goldhub/research/gold-market-commentary-may-2026?utm_source=openai))  
- **At these levels, valuation is sensitive to real yields.** Gold has no cash flow, so “undervalued” is harder to define than with stocks or bonds. If real yields stay elevated, gold can look expensive even if the long-term thesis is intact.
- **Central-bank buying can be price-sensitive.** Strong official demand supports gold, but if prices rise too far too fast, some buyers may slow purchases or some holders may sell into strength.

### My base view
I would call gold **fairly valued to somewhat rich in the short term**, but **not structurally overvalued** if your macro view includes weaker fiat confidence, persistent geopolitical risk, and continued central-bank accumulation.

A reasonable investor takeaway:

- **0–5% allocation:** fine for conservative portfolios that don’t want much commodity exposure.  
- **5–10% allocation:** reasonable if you want a meaningful inflation/geopolitical hedge.  
- **Above 10%:** starts to become a macro bet, not just diversification.

If you’re looking to buy today, I’d prefer **staggered buying** rather than a lump sum. Gold may still have upside, but it no longer looks like an obvious bargain.
